*Unitree's humanoid hit 12.66 meters per second, edging Usain Bolt's peak. Then one sprinted straight into an electrical box and threw sparks across the floor.*

The number is self-reported, and the prototype has no hands at all, because hands don't make you faster. Every gram went into *going*. Nobody built the part that *stops*.

What you'll learn:
✅ Why the *crash* explains every AI failure of the last two years
✅ The three *brakes* worth building into any system you run
✅ Human at the decision, not at the keyboard

The reason they left the hands off is the actual point of this whole thing.
